# numerical: simulate and compare with the exact answer

These tests compute what the theory promises (an error below ε, a circuit equal to a product formula, which
method is cheapest at equal accuracy) and compare with an exact or independent computation on a stated domain.
A pass is **empirical** on that domain; a case that fails is a counterexample.

Shared code: `_accuracy.py` (exact evolutions and errors), `_equal_accuracy.py` (cost rankings).

<!-- tests:begin (generated by `dagtool readmes`; edit the test docstrings, not this table) -->
| Test | What it checks | A pass grants |
|---|---|---|
| [`numerical/equal_accuracy`](equal_accuracy.py) | Which method needs the fewest vertices at the same accuracy ε. | Empirical on the cases listed. |
| [`numerical/hamsim_accuracy`](hamsim_accuracy.py) | The repetitions the theory gives reach accuracy ε, checked against e^{-iHt}. | Empirical on the domain. |
| [`numerical/trotter_circuit`](trotter_circuit.py) | The Trotter circuit implements the product formula it stands for. | Empirical on the cases listed. |
<!-- tests:end -->
